question: Under North Dakota's child care center rules (N.D. Admin. Code ch. 75-03-10), how many children less than eighteen months of age may one staff member care for at a licensed child care center in North Dakota?
quote: For children less than eighteen months of age, one staff member may care for four children, a ratio of .25 in decimal form, with a maximum group size of ten children;
notes: Maximum group size is 10. A mixed-age group that includes children under 18 months is capped at 10 (75-03-10-08(2)(b)(2)).

question: Under North Dakota's child care center rules (N.D. Admin. Code ch. 75-03-10), how many children aged three years to four years may one staff member care for at a licensed child care center in North Dakota?
quote: For children three years of age to four years of age, one staff member may care for seven children, a ratio of .14 in decimal form, with a maximum group size of twenty children;
notes: Maximum group size is 20.

question: Under North Dakota's child care center rules (N.D. Admin. Code ch. 75-03-10), how many children aged four years to five years may one staff member care for at a licensed child care center in North Dakota?
quote: For children four years of age to five years of age, one staff member may care for ten children, a ratio of .10 in decimal form, with a maximum group size of twenty-five children;
notes: Maximum group size is 25.

question: Under North Dakota's child care center rules (N.D. Admin. Code ch. 75-03-10), how many children aged six to twelve years may one staff member care for at a licensed child care center in North Dakota?
quote: For children six years to twelve years of age, one staff member may care for twenty children, a ratio of .05 in decimal form, with a maximum group size of forty children.
notes: Maximum group size is 40. Children five to six years: 1:12, group of 30.

question: Under North Dakota's child care center rules (N.D. Admin. Code ch. 75-03-10), what is the maximum group size for children aged four years to five years at a licensed child care center in North Dakota?
quote: For children four years of age to five years of age, one staff member may care for ten children, a ratio of .10 in decimal form, with a maximum group size of twenty-five children;
notes: Mixed-age groups take the group size of the majority age or of the youngest age group (75-03-10-08(2)(b)(1)). Centers serving only drop-in children are exempt from group-size limits (75-03-10-24(4)(a)).

question: What is the minimum age for a staff member responsible for caring for or teaching children at a licensed child care center in North Dakota?
quote: Shall be at least fourteen years of age, provided that each staff member under age sixteen has written parental consent for employment as a staff member
notes: Staff under 16 need written parental consent, and employment must comply with N.D.C.C. ch. 34-07. The operator must make sure staff under 18 are supervised by an adult staff member (75-03-10-09(17)).

question: Under North Dakota's child care center rules (N.D. Admin. Code ch. 75-03-10), a director of a licensed child care center in North Dakota who qualifies with an associate's degree in early childhood education or child development must also have at least how many months of experience in a child care center or similar setting?
quote: An associate's degree in the field of early childhood education or child development with at least six months of experience in a child care center or similar setting;
notes: This is one of seven alternative qualifications (75-03-10-10(3)(a)–(g)). For example, a bachelor's degree in early childhood education or child development needs no added experience. Directors must also certify 13 hours of approved training a year (75-03-10-10(4)).

question: How many hours of department-approved training must a staff member who works thirty or more hours per week at a licensed child care center in North Dakota certify each year?
quote: If working thirty or more hours ... department-approved training annually; ... per ... week, ... certify ... thirteen
notes: Fewer than 30 and more than 20 hours a week: 11 hours. 10 to 20 hours: 9. Under 10 hours: 7. The PDF lays this line out in columns, so the quote follows the extracted text order. Includes one hour on safe sleep (before caring for infants) and one hour on mandated reporting.

question: What is the minimum indoor space per child required at a licensed child care center in North Dakota?
quote: Adequate space must include a minimum of thirty-five square feet [3.25 square meters] of space per child indoors
notes: Excludes bathrooms, pantries, passageways to outdoor exits, areas under furniture or appliances children should not play on or under, and space children may not use.

question: What is the minimum outdoor play space per child required at a licensed child care center in North Dakota?
quote: a minimum of seventy-five square feet [6.97 square meters] of play space per child outdoors.
notes: Space must serve the licensed capacity. If the outdoor area cannot hold the licensed capacity at one time, it must be at least 75 sq ft times the number of children in the largest class or group. Centers with 75 sq ft per child of separate indoor recreation space for the largest group are exempt.

question: What is the maximum temperature of the water in faucets used by children at a licensed child care center in North Dakota?
quote: The water in the faucets used by children may not exceed one hundred twenty degrees Fahrenheit [49.2 degrees Celsius].
notes: The center must also have hot and cold running water.

question: What must a licensed child care center in North Dakota obtain from a child's parent before dispensing medication to the child?
answer: Written permission to dispense the medication, along with proper instructions for giving it.
quote: Require written permission to dispense medication and proper instructions for the administration of medication obtained from the parent of a child in the child care center who requires medication
notes: Prescribed medication must also come with the medical provider's written dosage and storage instructions and be labeled with the child's name and date (75-03-10-26(7)(a)).

question: How often must fire and emergency evacuation drills be performed at a licensed child care center in North Dakota?
quote: Fire and emergency evacuation drills must be performed monthly.

question: In what position must infants initially be placed for sleep at a licensed child care center in North Dakota?
quote: The operator shall ensure that infants are placed on their back initially when sleeping to lower the risk of sudden infant death syndrome, unless the infant's parent has provided a note from the infant's medical provider specifying otherwise.
notes: Exception requires a note from the infant's medical provider. The infant's face must stay uncovered.

question: Within what time must a licensed child care center in North Dakota report to the department an injury to a child in its care that requires medical treatment?
quote: Report to the department within twenty-four hours: ... An injury to any child which occurs while the child is in the care of the child care center and which requires medical treatment;
notes: The same 24-hour deadline covers a death, serious accident or illness requiring hospitalization, poisonings or medication errors, emergency closures or relocations, and fires or explosions (75-03-10-09(19)).

question: What immunization record must the operator of a licensed child care center in North Dakota maintain for each child?
answer: Verification that the child has received all age-appropriate immunizations, or a document on file stating the child is medically exempt or exempt based on religious, philosophical, or moral beliefs.
quote: Verification that the child has received all immunizations appropriate for the child's age, as prescribed by the public health division of the department, or have on file a document stating that the child is medically exempt or exempt from immunizations based on religious, philosophical, or moral beliefs
notes: The rule sets no deadline for this record. The health assessment is obtained at initial enrollment (75-03-10-22(2)(g)).

question: Within how many days of employment must each staff member responsible for caring for or teaching children at a licensed child care center in North Dakota be currently certified in pediatric first aid?
quote: Shall be currently certified within ninety days of employment and prior to staff member having unsupervised access to children under care, in pediatric first aid by a program approved by the department;
notes: Certification is also required before the staff member has unsupervised access to children. The same deadline applies to infant and pediatric CPR and AED certification (75-03-10-12(1)(d)).

question: What is the minimum aisle space between beds, cots, mats, cribs, and portable cribs at a licensed child care center in North Dakota?
quote: That aisles between beds, cots, mats, cribs, and portable cribs are a minimum space of two feet [60.96 centimeters] and are kept free of all obstructions while beds, cots, mats, cribs, and portable cribs are occupied.
notes: Aisles must also be kept free of obstructions while occupied.

question: Under North Dakota's child care center rules (N.D. Admin. Code ch. 75-03-10), a provisional license for a licensed child care center in North Dakota must expire at a set date no more than how many months after it is issued?
quote: A provisional license must: ... Expire at a set date, not to exceed six months from the date of issuance
notes: The chapter does not state the term of a regular license. An unrestricted license exchanged for a provisional one expires one year from the provisional license's issue date (75-03-10-06(2)(d)).

question: When children aged zero to eighteen months are in a mixed-age group in the same room at a licensed child care center in North Dakota, what is the maximum group size?
quote: When children age zero to eighteen months are in the mixed-age group, the maximum group size does not exceed ten children;
notes: A mixed-age group that already has the maximum children per staff member may add only older children (75-03-10-08(2)(b)(4)).

question: Under North Dakota's child care center rules (N.D. Admin. Code ch. 75-03-10), when a licensed child care center in North Dakota works out the staff needed for a mixed-age group and the total comes to 2.30 staff members, must it round up to 3 staff members?
quote: any fractional staff member count is then rounded to the next highest whole number whenever the fractional staff member count amounts to thirty-five hundredths or more. If lower than thirty-five hundredths, the fractional amount is dropped.
notes: Fractions of .35 or more round up; fractions below .35 are dropped, so 2.30 means 2 staff. Each age category's count is multiplied by its decimal ratio (e.g., .25 for under 18 months) and the results are added.

question: How long must an operator have been licensed before applying for a waiver of the required staff ratio and maximum group size for a licensed child care center in North Dakota?
quote: An operator licensed for at least two years may apply for a waiver of the required ratio and maximum group size, not to exceed .25 decimal point per group.
notes: A waiver may not exceed .25 decimal point per group and is reviewed every year. Denying or revoking a waiver cannot be appealed.

question: When a licensed child care center in North Dakota operating under a provisional license shows compliance and exchanges it for an unrestricted license, when does the unrestricted license expire?
answer: One year from the date the provisional license was issued.
quote: Be exchanged for an unrestricted license, which bears an expiration date of one year from the date of issuance of the provisional license
notes: The year runs from the provisional license's issue date, not from the exchange date.

question: Within what time must a licensed child care center in North Dakota inform parents in writing of first aid given to their child?
quote: Require that the child care center inform parents in writing of any first aid administered to their child within twenty-four hours of the incident
notes: Parents must be notified immediately of any injury needing emergency care beyond first aid, and each injury report goes in the child's record.
